transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-04
Start: 09:30 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Laura Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood Solutions), Maya Alvarez (BrightNote Head of Search), Daniel Kim (BrightNote ML Eng), Priya Shah (BrightNote PM), Alex Turner (BrightNote Eng Manager)

Summary (auto): Redwood walkthrough of Hosted API embeddings and rerank endpoint with example search workflow. Customer wants better relevance without huge infra lift; interested in quick pilot.

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you carving time. Quick intros then we'll jump into a short demo of the hosted embeddings endpoint and our rerank flow, and then leave time for questions.
[00:18] Maya (BrightNote): Thanks Samir. We're excited — we want to improve our search relevance for article recommendations, low latency, and keep costs reasonable.
[00:28] Laura (Redwood): Great — I'll share my screen in a sec. Quick context check: are you still running Elastic as primary search with FAISS/annoy for embeddings?
[00:36] Daniel (BrightNote): Yeah that's the stack — Elastic for filtering + BM25, and we use FAISS for vector recall. Rerank is currently a lightweight logistic model, struggling with edge cases.
[00:48] Priya (BrightNote): Also timeline: Q1 push for improved CTR on homepage. We're evaluating hosted options first.
[00:56] Samir (Redwood): Perfect — that's exactly the sort of workload Redwood's hosted API helps with: generate embeddings, run ANN to get candidates, then call a rerank endpoint for final scoring. I'll hand it to Laura for the walkthrough.
[01:05] Laura (Redwood): Cool. Sharing screen now — this is the Redwood Console. Top-left is the model catalog, we have curated embedding models tuned for semantic search and lightweight vectors. On the right you'll see example calls.
[01:20] Laura (Redwood): For hosted embeddings, it's a single endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings with model param. We return a vector and metadata. Example: we call model "redwood-search-embedding-22k" which outputs 1536 dims for higher recall.
[01:35] Daniel (BrightNote): 1536 — that's similar to ours. How do you handle dimensionality mismatch if we already have 768-dim vectors?
[01:43] Laura (Redwood): You can either reindex with our embeddings or use a lower-dim model. We also support custom quantization and dimensionality reduction guidance in the Console Optimize tab; for pilots we recommend reembedding the corpus for consistent space — it improves rerank signal.
[02:00] Maya (BrightNote): What's the latency on the embeddings call? We're doing thousands of queries per minute at peak.
[02:07] Laura (Redwood): For the hosted API, typical p95 for single embedding call is ~30-60ms depending on model size and region; batch endpoints are available to amortize overhead. For throughput we can recommend batching or using our dedicated pools.
[02:20] Samir (Redwood): Also you'll see in the Console Optimize we provide batching/caching suggestions and expected cost delta. We'll send your team a tailored recommendation after we see sample logs.
[02:33] Diego (Redwood): Important to note the rerank endpoint is where you get per-candidate neural scoring. The flow we demo: query -> embeddings -> ANN -> get top N candidates -> POST /v1/rerank with the query + candidates -> get final scores and ordering.
[02:47] Priya (BrightNote): So rerank runs on the hosted inference path — are documents sent to Redwood? Data residency question.
[02:55] Samir (Redwood): Good callout. For hosted we offer options: transient-only retention for inference (we don't store inputs by default), SOC 2 controls, and customer can opt for dedicated capacity or Private for strict residency. We'll attach the security pack.
[03:10] Maya (BrightNote): Can you show an example rerank payload?
[03:15] Laura (Redwood): Sure — I'll switch to the API playground. Example payload: { query: "...", candidates: [{id: 123, text: "..."}, ...] } — we return scores and reasons. Here's a notebook snippet where we compute query embedding, fetch ANN candidates from your store, then call rerank with the candidate texts and ID.
[03:38] Laura (Redwood): (typing) Example code — python requests POST to /v1/rerank, body includes query_embedding optional or raw query text; we support both. If you supply embeddings, rerank skips re-embedding and saves ~20ms per candidate set.
[03:55] Daniel (BrightNote): That embedding pass-through is useful. How does rerank scale with N? We usually retrieve top 200 then rerank top 20.
[04:04] Laura (Redwood): Rerank is linear in the number of candidates you send; we optimize kernels for batch scoring — sending 20 per request is the common sweet spot. If you send 200 we can still handle it, but cost and latency grow. We can also use a hybrid approach: cheap lexical boosts then rerank a small set.
[04:22] Alex (BrightNote): Any limits on payload size for rerank? We include metadata and some HTML sometimes.
[04:29] Laura (Redwood): We recommend stripping heavy HTML, send text excerpts. We have a 256KB request cap for hosted by default; for special cases we can adjust via dedicated.
[04:40] Maya (BrightNote): Can you share numbers on recall/CTR improvement customers have seen using rerank?
[04:46] Samir (Redwood): Anecdotally, customers switching from BM25+ANN to ANN+neural rerank see 6-15% CTR lift on relevance-focused pages. We'll include anonymized case studies in the follow-up.
[04:58] Priya (BrightNote): How do you handle A/B tests and rollouts? We need to gradually roll the model.
[05:05] Diego (Redwood): Console supports A/B rollouts for rerank models — you can run canary traffic, compare metrics, and automatically rollback. Also built-in tracing ties back to per-query latency and token cost.
[05:18] Daniel (BrightNote): About cost — token-based for rerank? Or per-request?
[05:23] Samir (Redwood): For hosted, embeddings are per-embedding unit and rerank is per-request + per-token when applicable. We'll send a pricing sheet with examples using your estimated query volume to model cost.
[05:35] Maya (BrightNote): Security — we need SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs, KMS integration.
[05:42] Samir (Redwood): We are SOC 2 compliant and support SAML/SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC in Console, and KMS/HSM integrations on Private. Hosted also supports encrypted in-transit and at-rest keys managed by Redwood; dedicated/private gives you customer-managed keys. Full details in the security pack we'll share.
[05:59] Priya (BrightNote): Good. Could you run through a small end-to-end demo with a sample query?
[06:04] Laura (Redwood): Absolutely. I'll use a small sample corpus — the steps are: 1) call embeddings for the query, 2) ANN search to fetch top candidates (we'll simulate using our in-console mini-ann), 3) call rerank and return final ordering.
[06:18] [screen content, demo running]
[06:25] Laura (Redwood): (demo) Query: "how to increase newsletter CTR" — ANN gives five candidates. Now hitting rerank, returning scores and a small explanation field for why a doc scored higher (keywords + semantic similarity). Notice the ordering changed to surface a practical how-to guide that previously ranked low.
[06:45] Maya (BrightNote): Nice, that example maps to what we see — the logistic model misses phrasing nuances.
[06:51] Daniel (BrightNote): Can rerank incorporate features like click-through history or recency?
[06:56] Laura (Redwood): Rerank supports supplementary features — you can pass numeric features per candidate and we use them in the final scoring. Many customers add click_rate, publish_date_delta, personalization signals.
[07:09] Priya (BrightNote): What about cold-start/new articles?
[07:12] Laura (Redwood): We recommend combining BM25 boosts + embeddings and using sparse-dense hybrid. Our Optimize tab can show which documents are underperforming and suggest reindex cadence.
[07:24] Alex (BrightNote): On the infra side, can we run the ANN in our env and only call Redwood for embeddings and rerank?
[07:30] Samir (Redwood): Yes — that's a common setup: you keep ANN in your infra for control, send only candidate texts/ids for rerank to Redwood. For high privacy, you can use Private or Dedicated.
[07:42] Maya (BrightNote): For the pilot, we'd prefer to keep vectors in-house but test rerank on hosted first. Is that OK?
[07:48] Samir (Redwood): Totally fine and fast to evaluate. For the pilot we'll provide code samples to call rerank and to securely upload candidates.
[07:57] Daniel (BrightNote): How about evaluation harness? We have labeled relevance ratings for 5k queries — can Redwood run offline evals?
[08:03] Diego (Redwood): Yes, we have an evals module. For pilots we usually run your labeled set through both your baseline and our rerank pipeline and share precision/recall/ndcg metrics. We'll need the dataset in the agreed format.
[08:17] Priya (BrightNote): Ok — logistics: what are the timelines and what do we need to provide to kick off?
[08:22] Samir (Redwood): Proposed flow: 1) BrightNote shares sample logs and the labeled eval set; 2) Redwood spins up a short pilot, reembeds a small subset (or you keep vectors in-house), runs rerank experiments, and returns metrics in ~2 weeks. We'll send a pilot scoping doc.
[08:36] Maya (BrightNote): That timeline works. Budget owners will want a ballpark cost before commit.
[08:40] Samir (Redwood): We'll include scoped cost estimates in the pricing doc — both hosted and dedicated options.
[08:46] Daniel (BrightNote): A few technical Qs: 1) Do you support batching embeddings to reduce RPC overhead? 2) Any SDKs? 3) Do you have latency SLAs for hosted?
[08:55] Laura (Redwood): 1) Yes, batch embeddings endpoint exists; 2) SDKs for Python/Node — examples in the Console; 3) Hosted has best-effort latency guarantees, dedicated offers SLA-backed latency and uptime.
[09:06] Alex (BrightNote): Can you show the Optimize tab recommendations?
[09:10] Laura (Redwood): Sure— switching to Optimize. Here you see recommendations: 1) use small batch size of 8 for embeddings to balance latency and throughput; 2) cache common query prefixes; 3) quantize embeddings to int8 for cold storage — improves storage and retrieval cost. There's an estimated cost delta next to each suggestion.
[09:27] Priya (BrightNote): Quantization—does that affect rerank quality?
[09:30] Laura (Redwood): Slightly for extreme quantization but our recommendations are conservative for production (8-bit) and we show expected NDCG delta from a sample dataset. For rerank we use float tensors in memory so quantization is mainly for store.
[09:44] Maya (BrightNote): Any compliance limitations — we have EU users and data residency requirements.
[09:49] Samir (Redwood): We support region pinning for hosted, and Private for strict residency. We'll note EU region options in the follow-up.
[09:59] Daniel (BrightNote): If we keep ANN in-house, what does the integration look like? Do you provide a client lib to call rerank and map ids?
[10:06] Laura (Redwood): We provide SDK helpers and examples: compute query embedding, fetch top-k ids from your index, retrieve lightweight candidate payloads, call rerank. Mapping is by candidate id. We also provide a benchmark harness you can run locally.
[10:18] Maya (BrightNote): Good. Any shared artifacts you can send?
[10:21] Samir (Redwood): We'll send: security pack, pricing + hosted vs dedicated comparison, pilot scoping doc, and sample notebook with rerank flow.
[10:30] Priya (BrightNote): Sounds good. Quick question on retraining / model updates for rerank — how does model versioning work?
[10:37] Diego (Redwood): Console has model versioning and rollout controls. You can pin a model to a route, run canary percent, and rollback. We also store inference metrics per model.
[10:47] Daniel (BrightNote): For internal audits, we need request logs mapped by team — is that supported?
[10:52] Samir (Redwood): Yep — audit logs and request tracing are available; for hosted we retain per-account logs per retention policy; dedicated/private can have extended retention.
[11:03] [short pause while Laura pulls up notebook]
[11:10] Laura (Redwood): One more demo snippet — here's a quick Jupyter cell showing the whole flow: call embeddings (30ms), call ANN locally (internal), call rerank (70ms p95 for 20 candidates). We're in the same ballpark as your requirements.
[11:30] Alex (BrightNote): 70ms p95 is acceptable for our homepage? We target under 150ms end-to-end for the search page.
[11:35] Laura (Redwood): With caching and batching, plus local ANN, you should comfortably stay under 150ms end-to-end. We'll help tune those knobs.
[11:46] Maya (BrightNote): Anything we should watch out for when reembedding old content?
[11:50] Diego (Redwood): Reembedding large corpora is I/O intensive; we provide parallel workers and recommend incremental reindexing. We'll provide guidance for a zero-downtime migration plan.
[12:01] Priya (BrightNote): Ok can we recap next concrete items?
[12:05] Samir (Redwood): Sure — recap: 1) Redwood sends pricing, security pack, pilot scope + sample notebook (Samir) by 2025-11-06; 2) BrightNote shares 1k anonymized queries and the labeled eval set (Daniel) by 2025-11-10; 3) Redwood runs offline evals and spins pilot (Laura + Diego) with results in ~2 weeks; 4) schedule infra deep-dive with Laura and Daniel week of 2025-11-10.
[12:33] Maya (BrightNote): That works. Thanks, team.
[12:36] Samir (Redwood): Great — we'll follow up with calendar invites. Any final Qs?
[12:40] Priya (BrightNote): None from me.
[12:42] Daniel (BrightNote): Nope. Thanks.
[12:44] Samir (Redwood): Thanks everyone — talk soon.
